title: Exploring the Boundaries of Content Moderation in Text-to-Image Generation

bias_targets.methodology: Auditing content moderation in T2I models by calculating the censorship rate of prompts describing stigmatized physical traits (e.g., obesity, severe acne, tattoos).
Auditing content moderation in T2I models by calculating the censorship rate of prompts describing stigmatized health conditions (e.g., HIV/AIDS, leprosy, mental health issues).

Auditing content moderation in T2I models by calculating the censorship rate of prompts related to women's physiological processes (e.g., menstruation, breastfeeding, menopause) and gender non-conforming appearances.
Auditing content moderation in T2I models by calculating the censorship rate of prompts describing low socioeconomic status (e.g., poverty, homelessness, debt).
Auditing content moderation in T2I models by calculating the censorship rate of prompts describing specific ethnic groups (e.g., Uighur, Rohingya) and religious attire/practices.
Auditing content moderation in T2I models by calculating the censorship rate of prompts describing specific political ideologies (e.g., communism, fascism) and figures.
Auditing content moderation in T2I models by calculating the censorship rate of prompts describing non-normative relationship structures (e.g., polyamory) and LGBTQ+ advocacy.

Auditing content moderation in T2I models by calculating the censorship rate of prompts describing stigmatized occupations (e.g., sex work, janitorial work) versus illegal but romanticized roles (e.g., mafia boss).
